Subject: SIG: BCDR rehearsal & RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the packet you sent last week. As part of HorizonCare's SIG review we're looking to validate Redwood's business continuity controls for production inference (hosted) and confirm evidence around your recent rehearsal. Specifically we need: 

- RTO and RPO targets for hosted API endpoints and any differences for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Backup cadence, retention, and encryption details for model artifacts, KV caches, and customer data stored for inference (if any).
- Cross-region failover approach and how automatic routing/backfill works when a region is degraded.
- Evidence of the last full rehearsal (date, scope, attendee list, outcomes) and any postmortem notes.

Can you provide concise answers and any artifacts (playbook excerpt, backup summary, rehearsal attestation) by Dec 10? We have a HorizonCare internal rehearsal approval on Dec 21 and would like to align schedules.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Senior IT Risk Analyst
HorizonCare

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary answers below and I attached the playbook excerpt and backup summary as separate files (redwood_bcdr_playbook_v2.pdf, backup_policy_summary.xlsx) plus the attestation from our last rehearsal (rehearsal_attestation_2026-11-15.pdf). See also the Drive link in the metadata for the full runbook.

High-level answers (concise):

- RTO / RPO
  - Hosted API (critical inference paths): RTO target = 15 minutes for control-plane failover and traffic cutover to a healthy region; RPO = 1 hour for application-level state that we persist (e.g., customer-uploaded artifacts). Note: ephemeral token/stream state is not long-lived and has no formal backup.
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): RTO target = 30 minutes for tenant-level failover when using cross-region warm-standby; RPO = 4 hours for tenant-managed datasets that are replicated by customer request.
  - Private/on-prem: RTO/RPO are subject to the customer's topology and SLAs; we provide guidance in the playbook.

- Backups and retention
  - Artifact backups: daily full backup + hourly incremental for config and model artifacts; incremental retention = 30 days, full backup retention = 90 days for standard retention.
  - Audit/log retention: system logs retained 7 years (long-term retention available as an add-on).
  - Encryption: all backups encrypted at rest with AES-256 and keys managed via our KMS/HSM integrations. Data-in-transit uses TLS 1.3.
  - Storage: backups are stored across two regions by default (us-west1, us-east1) with immutable snapshots for the retention window.

- Cross-region failover
  - Smart routing + prefix/KV cache population: traffic is routed by our smart-router which prefers local region but will fail over to pre-warmed capacity in the secondary region. We rehydrate prefix caches from immutable snapshots and replay short-lived caches where possible; cold-cache impact during the first few minutes is expected.
  - Automatic fallbacks: our policy engine will route to a compatible quantized variant if the preferred model is unavailable to preserve throughput.

- Rehearsal evidence (attached)
  - Last full rehearsal: 2026-11-15 (canary + partial regional failover). Scope: API ingress failover, cache replay test, and traffic validation for our top 10 customer routes.
  - Outcome: cutover completed in 12 minutes for the critical path; two minor regressions (metric collection lag, a config flag mismatch) were fixed within the postmortem.
  - Attestation: signed by On-call and SRE lead (file attached).

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- We ran a canary on 2026-11-15 (attached attestation). We propose a full dress rehearsal on 2026-12-22 02:00–04:00 PT (low-traffic window). If that timing works for HorizonCare, we can add you to the observer list and share the short play-by-play.

If you want, Karthik can provide a short distilled single-page summary of recovery steps for your board.

Best,
Camila Reyes

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: BCDR rehearsal & RTO/RPO clarifications

Looping in a quick note for clarity —

Two internal clarifications to add before we send the final artifacts to HorizonCare:

1) Dedicated customers: emphasize that Dedicated customers who opt into cross-region replication have a warm-standby configuration and their effective RTO is our 30-minute target when the customer has enabled replication. If they have single-region Dedicated with no replication, RTO is region-dependent and recovery will involve rebuild/restore.

2) Data classification: we should call out in the playbook excerpt that customer PII/phs data follows additional retention rules; for customers requiring longer RPO we recommend enabling continuous replication add-on (sales-approved).

Camila, small edits in the playbook doc are in the Drive folder (I added the Dedicated note and the PII paragraph).

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — the summary and attachments look good and answer most of our SIG questions. A few follow-ups before we close our control evidence:

- Please confirm the full dress rehearsal on 2026-12-22 is on and whether HorizonCare is permitted to observe (read-only).
- One-line recovery summary: could you send a single paragraph we can share with our Compliance Board summarizing the automated failover and the expected impact on in-flight requests?

If you can get the two-signer attestation and the one-line summary by EOD Dec 23 we can mark this control as evidence-ready and close it in our SIG tracker.

Appreciate it —
Jordan Ellis
Senior IT Risk Analyst
HorizonCare
